structured_output.summary: The correction closes the sole P1 causally and stays inside the authorized surface. The blocking finding was that `createDirectRoomHeadControl()` holds the floor in memory (entry asset:870-872) and `directPendingRecovery()` hands the identical `control` object to both the pre-crash room (:1189) and the "reopened" room (:1203), so no restart ever exercises a surviving floor. The corrected plan replaces this for the new fixture with one origin-scoped IndexedDB-backed provider whose every write originates from the real room's create/begin/commit, bans the parent and fixture from constructing, replacing, normalizing, or mutating a stable/pending value after the crash, and requires the newly launched Chromium process to instantiate a fresh provider, reread the floor verbatim, and prove reread canonical bytes and digest equal the pre-crash begin result before the room opens. That is durability plus non-authorship, which is exactly the disjunction the P1 named. Feasibility is confirmed at the contract: `V3RoomHeadAuthority` is an exported interface injected through the required `roomHeadAuthority` input (index.ts:270-285, :388, entry asset:1035), the asset already drives raw IndexedDB (`openExistingDatabase`/`request`/`transactionDone`), and `{kind:"reopen"}` is a mode selector routed to `read()` (index.ts:920-922), not floor content — so no production, API, schema, dependency, or authority-semantic change is implied. Fresh-process causality holds: the existing persistent-profile children spawn a genuine new OS process via `launchPersistentContext`, and `rawSnapshotDeclaration()` already derives the declaration purely from the durable snapshot-quarantine database, so local rederivation is real rather than parent-injected. The RED binding is deterministic on inspection: the epoch-0/1 pins in `authenticatePendingCandidate()` (creator-adoption.ts:1305-1386) reject every generation at epoch 2→3, yielding `pending-missing` (:1468), which falls outside the pending-invalid set and maps to room-level `D110C_FLOOR_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` (index.ts:2203-2206) in both crash orderings. The GREEN bindings cite seams that genuinely exist — `currentProjectionKind()`, `openCreatorCheckpointTrust()` with `expectedCurrentHead`, `inspectCreatorTransitionAdvance(mode:"verify")`, and the cold-reopen owner's current-projection epoch/objectId/blueprint checks (:1041-1075) — and the added projection binding is what defeats same-kind generation-2 substitution once current and successor projections share a kind at N>=1. The epoch-N deferral is both explicit and structurally necessary: the epoch-1 reopen pin (index.ts:1576) is guarded by `pending === null`, so the crash-restart path legitimately bypasses it while a completed `{stable: 3, pending: null}` reopen cannot, and that case is assigned to D.110c-c as blocking before its post-adoption restart gate. The slice is not weakened, because the pre-crash setup reaches stable epoch 2 without any reopen: `performCreatorSuccessorAdoption()` rebinds a fresh close handle in-session (:3629-3637), matching the scope line that excludes only a third completed hot transition. Scope and evidence are preserved: the commit contains 31 new files and exactly one modified file, no production or test source changed, no prior evidence rewritten (the immutable Grok packet's trailing space was preserved rather than reformatted), publish then floor-commit then cold-open ordering is intact (index.ts:2182-2211), and the retained 0→1 matrix keeps its in-memory provider untouched. The blocking union is closed; three P2s are recorded and do not trigger another plan round.

findings.title: Room-level RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE does not by itself distinguish pending-missing from storage-failed or pending-old
findings.evidence: The plan pins the RED to room-level `D110C_FLOOR_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` "corresponding to the current pending authenticator's `pending-missing` result". But examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2202-2206 routes only kind in {true-fork, chain-invalid, stale-head, malformed-input} to PENDING_INVALID and collapses every other kind — including `storage-failed` (creator-adoption.ts:1452) and `pending-old` (:1505, :1509) — into RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE. The room throws a bare TypeError carrying only the code (index.ts:804-806), so the fixture cannot read `recoveredPending.kind` through the room path. A fixture that silently lost the durable head would produce the same observable token as the intended missing seam.
findings.required_action: During RED, additionally observe the authenticator kind directly — the exported `@ts-drp/node/creator-adoption-recover` boundary is side-effect-free in this scenario because candidates.length === 0 returns before any swapHead — or serialize the durable head, lineage, and Cut/QC/trust/projection presence so storage-failed and pending-old are positively excluded rather than merely asserted. No plan round required.

findings.title: Local snapshot-declaration rederivation helper is hard-pinned to exactly one verified scope
findings.evidence: The plan requires the newly launched process to locally re-derive the snapshot declaration. The existing helper `rawSnapshotDeclaration()` filters scopes to `state === "verified"` and throws "D.108d2 snapshot scope is ambiguous" unless exactly one remains (:749-751). After 0→1, 1→2, and the staged 2→3 transition in one persistent profile there will be more than one verified scope, so the mandated local rederivation cannot use the helper as written.
findings.required_action: Generalize the helper with an epoch selector, mirroring the existing `rawAuthorityAtEpoch(databaseName, epoch)` / `rawAuthority()` split at :700-738. Test-asset-only work inside the already authorized surface; resolve during RED.

findings.title: The one-shot commit fault seam is in-memory and does not carry across a process kill as-is
findings.evidence: The plan states the RED "uses the already retained `failBeforePublication` and one-shot room-head commit fault seams". The commit seam's one-shot semantics are implemented by mutating in-memory state — `if (operation === "commit" && control.fault === "commit-unavailable-once") { control.fault = "none"; ... }` (:887-890) — which is meaningless once the Chromium process is killed. Reuse is therefore partial rather than literal.
findings.required_action: Express the new-AHE ordering's commit fault as pre-crash configuration on the durable provider (fail the commit, then terminate; no reset needed), and do not rely on the in-memory reset path. Test-asset-only; resolve during RED.
